clue.text: Sort of diet meeting the needs of the local community

definitions.text: Sort of diet meeting the needs of the local community

parts.words: Sort of diet meeting the needs of the local community
parts.note: a diet is also a formal assembly, so this describes an elected body serving a locality, not a food plan

explanation.surface: A nutritionist recommends an eating regime suited to what a neighbourhood needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diet' tempts toward food; here it is the old word for a legislative assembly, and the meeting is a local government body. In Britain this is the tier of local government below the county.
explanation.definitionFit: A local authority body is an assembly, which is the old parliamentary sense of a diet, serving a community.

clue.text: In company here you'll be waiting for a rise

definitions.text: In company here you'll be waiting for a rise

parts.words: In company here you'll be waiting for a rise
parts.note: an airport room where travellers sit in a crowd until their plane takes off, the rise being a take-off rather than a pay rise

explanation.surface: An employee sits at the firm waiting for a salary increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In company' and 'rise' suggest an office worker hoping for more pay; the company is just other people, and the rise is an aircraft climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers gather in the airport waiting area before their flight climbs into the sky.

clue.text: Getting a recess is up to the student body

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is is written bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written before turning
NUS is the National Union of Students, the UK student organisation

explanation.surface: Whether a holiday break happens depends on the students' union.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' signals a reversal; 'is up' looks like 'depends on' in the surface. The NUS is Britain's National Union of Students.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinus is an anatomical cavity, a hollow or recess in bone.

clue.text: Ball game in the middle of the home is destructive

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the ball game
taken as written

indicators.note: only the central letters of the word for home are kept, its ends dropped

parts.note: a home is a house

explanation.surface: Playing a ball game indoors is wrecking the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the middle of' trims HOUSE to OUS. RU is the standard abbreviation for rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ruinous brings ruin, so it is destructive in effect.

clue.text: Grants society to replace right to admit

indicators.note: the letter for society goes in where the letter for right stood

parts.note: to grant something is to confer it

explanation.surface: A charitable society awards grants instead of righting wrongs, then owns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace right' swaps the R of CONFERS for S.
explanation.definitionFit: To confess is to own up to or acknowledge something, a synonym of admit.

clue.text: It's a c-crime to break up potter's object

indicators.note: breaking up the letters signals rearranging them

parts.note: the stammered c gives a second letter C

explanation.surface: Smashing a pot is a crime, the stuttering speaker says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break up' rearranges A plus CCRIME. The stammer is there only to supply the extra C.
explanation.definitionFit: Fired clay ware is what a potter makes, so a ceramic is a potter's piece.

clue.text: Supervised the game for two of 21?

definitions.text: Supervised the game for two of 21?

parts.words: Supervised the game for two of 21?
parts.note: the entry at 21 is cricket teams, so this is the official who controlled a match between two sides

explanation.surface: Someone oversaw a match between two of the teams named elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 21-down, cricket teams of eleven; a match between two of them has an official in white coat ruling on play.
explanation.definitionFit: To umpire is to officiate a match, deciding on rules between two sides.

clue.text: New Lyric has support initially; it's in the process of developing

definitions.text: it's in the process of developing

indicators.note: a new version of the words means their letters reshaped
only the opening letter of support is taken

explanation.surface: A fresh song lyric with backing is still being worked on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges LYRICHAS; 'initially' takes S from 'support' to end the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupa inside its case is the stage of an insect transforming into an adult.

clue.text: Highly value hypermarket in area at the side of the road

indicators.note: the store sits inside the roadside stopping place

parts.words: area at the side of the road
parts.note: a lay-by is a British roadside pull-in where cars can stop
a hypermarket is a very large shop, a great store

explanation.surface: A huge supermarket is put in a roadside parking spot, which planners prize.
explanation.walkthrough: A LAY-BY is a British pull-in at the edge of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: To set great store by something is an idiom for regarding it as very important.

clue.text: English person in work could finally be one

definitions.text: English person in work could finally be one

indicators.note: work used as a verb means knead or reshape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Englishman with a job may one day retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges E plus PERSON plus IN; read whole, the clue says a working English person will eventually draw a pension.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone retired who draws a state or company pension, as a worker eventually does.

clue.text: Standard lines of rebuff

parts.note: par is the standard score or level
RY is short for railway, lines of track

explanation.surface: A typical way of turning someone down.
explanation.walkthrough: RY for railway is a crossword convention for 'lines'.
explanation.definitionFit: To parry is to ward off or deflect a blow or question, as a rebuff does.

clue.text: SOS sent in anger: food item required

indicators.note: the jumbled distress call is placed inside the word for anger

parts.note: to rile is to anger

indicators.note: sent in the sense of carried away or transported, so the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: An angry distress signal goes out because someone needs food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent' rearranges SOS to SSO, which goes 'in' RILE; 'required' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fried cake of minced meat or fish coated in crumbs is a food item.

clue.text: Doctor's brighter, but lacking iodine becomes more gloomy

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: the chemical symbol is taken out of the comparative word

parts.note: rosier means brighter or more hopeful
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A medic seems cheerier, but without a mineral supplement he turns glum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking iodine' removes I from ROSIER, giving ROSER.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means sullen and gloomy, so the comparative form is gloomier.

clue.text: Runner performing in street, refusing bribe

indicators.note: the bribe word is turned away, its letters removed from the street performer's activity

parts.note: busking is playing music in the street for money
a bung is British slang for a bribe

explanation.surface: An athlete busks on the street but will not take a backhander.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking B, U, N and G out of BUSKING in order leaves the answer. BUNG is British slang for a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: The runners of a sledge are its skis, so a ski is a runner over snow.

clue.text: Man swimming in river, son reveals

indicators.note: the jumbled man goes inside the river

parts.note: the Usk is a river in Wales

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters move about

explanation.surface: A man swims in a river, and his son exposes something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' is the anagram signal, fitting the river scene, and 'in' places the jumbled man inside the Usk, a river in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: To unmask is to expose or reveal the true identity behind a disguise.

clue.text: Inferior cheese? A short time to consume some picked up

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time
to use is to consume

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for some is lifted, read bottom to top

parts.note: a part is some of something

explanation.surface: A poor cheese is one that is eaten partly in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' reverses PART to TRAP. Mousetrap is British slang for cheap, tasteless cheddar.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, cheap bland cheddar is called this, fit only to bait a trap.

clue.text: A take-off though lacking second gear

indicators.note: the letter for second is dropped from the parody word

parts.note: a skit is a parody, a take-off

explanation.surface: An aircraft taking off without a second gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking second' removes S from SKIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Kit is equipment or clothing for an activity, the same as gear.

clue.text: Sign at the bottom of a letter

definitions.text: Sign at the bottom of a letter

parts.words: Sign at the bottom of a letter
parts.note: not a signature closing a letter but a mark written under a single printed letter

explanation.surface: Signing your name at the foot of a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a signature at the end of correspondence; the letter is an alphabet character, and the sign is the hook under a c in French.
explanation.definitionFit: The hook placed under c in words like façade is a diacritic sitting beneath the letter.

clue.text: Look up and down

indicators.note: the word reads the same going up the grid as coming down

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Glance up and then down.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'up and down' says the answer reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look at it closely.

clue.text: Learned head leaves country, possibly tied

indicators.note: the leading letter of the country goes

parts.note: Peru is a South American country

indicators.note: possibly signals a different arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A leader quits the country, perhaps bound up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head leaves' takes P from PERU, giving ERU; 'possibly' rearranges TIED to DITE.
explanation.definitionFit: An erudite person is scholarly, having learned a great deal.

clue.text: Untidy place in line moving impressively

indicators.note: the pig pen goes inside the jumbled word
moving tells us the letters shift position

parts.note: a sty, a pigsty, is a filthy messy place

explanation.surface: A messy spot in the queue starts to move with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges LINE to INLE, and STY goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in style means doing it with flair and elegance, impressively.

clue.text: Teams in drinks break after last pair dismissed

indicators.note: the final two letters of the break word are removed

parts.note: elevenses is a British mid-morning break for tea or coffee

explanation.surface: Cricket sides break for drinks once the final batting pair is out.
explanation.walkthrough: ELEVENSES is the British mid-morning snack; dropping its final ES leaves the answer, cricket or football sides of eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: A side of eleven players in cricket or football is called an eleven.

clue.text: Removes from office when speed so critical

indicators.note: a critical state suggests upheaval, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ousting leaders when quickness is so important.
explanation.walkthrough: 'critical' rearranges SPEED and SO.
explanation.definitionFit: To depose a ruler is to oust them from power.

clue.text: Delegate seen briefly by river to get rid of insects

indicators.note: the word is cut short, keeping only its first few letters

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A delegate glimpsed beside a river is told to clear out the bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' shortens Delegate to DEL; the Ouse is a river in England.
explanation.definitionFit: To delouse means to remove lice, which are parasitic insects.

clue.text: Language uses wordplay to needle one

parts.note: a pun is play on words
a jab is an injection with a needle
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone uses a pun to get under another's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue spoken in the Punjab region of India and Pakistan.

clue.text: Fish comes back for shelter

indicators.note: returning means the fish word is read backwards

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A fish returns to cover.
explanation.definitionFit: The lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind.

clue.text: Be responsible for the show abroad, say

indicators.note: say indicates a word that sounds like the one wanted

parts.note: abroad means overseas

explanation.surface: Managing the touring production in a foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for abroad, spoken, gives the verb meaning supervise.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee a production is to supervise it, being in charge of it.

clue.text: It's no good one featuring in design of the past

indicators.note: the pieces appear inside the emblem word

parts.note: a logo is an emblem or design
A means one

explanation.surface: A worthless logo design from history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featuring in' is the container signal; 'It's' is a link, and the definition is an adjective phrase, as in 'long-ago days'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from a distant time is long-ago, belonging to the past.

clue.text: A farmer mainly very quick

indicators.note: mainly means most of the name, so its last letter goes

parts.note: Farmer Giles is the stock British name for a farmer

explanation.surface: A farmer who is mostly nimble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' drops the last letter of GILES. Farmer Giles is a stock comic name for a British farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile means nimble and quick-moving.

clue.text: Wyvern — not the first to be upset and easily disturbed

indicators.note: upset suggests the remaining letters are overturned and rearranged
the initial letter of the dragon's name is left out

explanation.surface: A heraldic dragon, not the leader, gets agitated and jumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first' removes W from Wyvern, and 'to be upset' rearranges YVERN.
explanation.definitionFit: A nervy person is jittery and anxious, readily disturbed.

clue.text: I've Act due to be reconsidered, relating to schooling

indicators.note: reconsidering suggests the letters are rethought into a new order

explanation.surface: An education act is up for review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be reconsidered' rearranges IVE, ACT and DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Educative means serving to educate, so it concerns teaching and schooling.

clue.text: Good service provided by fast bowler

definitions.meaning: a rapid postal or courier service delivering items quickly
in cricket a delivery is a ball bowled, and a fast bowler sends them down at great speed

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler's ball is a delivery, so a quick bowler is the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast courier option, and a quick ball from a cricket bowler.
